title: Guide: every optimal deletion set
description: As the fewest-deletions loop, but after the first solution a program part cap forbids larger deletion sets, and the loop lists every optimal one. See the guide page "Optimisation".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The Paley graph on n nodes (n a prime of the form 4m + 1): two nodes are joined when
% their difference is a square modulo n.
node(0..n-1).
square((X*X) \ n) :- X = 1..n-1.
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V, square((V-U) \ n).
fragments.description: The Paley graph on n nodes. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any set of nodes to delete, as few as possible.
{ del(V) : node(V) }.
#minimize { 1,V : del(V) }.
% The number of deletions.
size(N) :- N = #count { V : del(V) }.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any deletion set, fewest deletions first.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: c nodes that are not deleted and pairwise joined.
c { q(V) : node(V) } c.
:- q(V), del(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
#show q/1.

% The clique survives as long as none of its nodes is deleted.
relevant(del(V)) :- q(V).
fragments.description: Looks for a clique of c nodes that survives the deletions (solver C).

fragments.name: cap
fragments.text:
#program cap(i).
% best(i,size(B)): the fewest deletions are B. No larger set is of interest.
:- best(i,size(B)), size(N), N > B.
fragments.description: Grounded once, after the first solution: forbids larger deletion sets.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + cap
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# After the first solution, the part cap forbids larger deletion sets; the loop goes
# on and lists the others of the same size.
capped = false
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
        if not capped:
            A.expand(cap, best = M.atoms(size/1))
            capped = true
